instruction: I have jotted down my amazon shopping list in simple_note. Reset my amazon cart to have as many products in as many quantities from this list as available, and tell me its total cost. In calculating the total cost (i) only include the available items, and (ii) include tax, but not delivery fees as I will be using prime later.
notes: Two apps: simple_note (read the shopping list note) and amazon (reset cart, add items, read total). The note's entries are modeled as a fixed set of three product/quantity placeholders tied to the note by static facts (on-list, purchase-quantity); their values are filled at runtime from show_note and show_product (quantity = min(listed, in-stock); products that are unavailable are simply skipped at runtime, so the number of add_product_to_cart calls may be smaller). clear_cart resets the cart exactly once (precondition (not (cart-cleared))) and all adds require (cart-cleared), so the end state only differs in amazon.CartEntry. show_cart asserts (total-known)/(found-total); any later clear/add deletes (total-known), which forces the total to be read after the final add and before complete_task. The answer is the cart total including tax but excluding delivery fee. The object-specific in-cart goals cannot be referenced from the domain action, so complete_task's precondition carries the domain-level goal conditions (cart-cleared, total-known, found-total); the in-cart facts are enforced via the problem goal, and (not (task-completed)) on every other action keeps complete_task last.
